**Verdict: REVISE** (1 Must-Fix, 3 Should-Fix, 1 skip-reason flag). Every

### Must-Fix 1 (CONFIRMED at source) — the escalation channel was a digest queue

`_telegram_push` (`autonomous_session_watch.py:34555`) does not send: it
enqueues into `~/my-goat/scripts/notif_enqueue.sh`, whose header states it
appends to the outbox for "the next batched digest (default 3x/day)", and whose
own docstring justifies that routing because "gate notifications are
observability, not time-critical", naming "the tick-side PushNotification" as
the second channel. NEITHER premise holds for this pass: a fleet-wide daemon
outage IS time-critical, and there is no tick-side second channel — per-issue
tick sessions spawn through the very daemon that is down. Worst-case digest
latency (~8h) EXCEEDS the 3h17m motivating outage, so a digest-only route
would have surfaced LATER than the human PM detection at 22:48Z that this pass
is meant to replace — defeating the plan's own Requirement sentence while
still satisfying its acceptance criteria (which counted enqueues, not
surfacing).

**Applied (v3):** episode **`open` + `recovered`** route through the immediate
`~/my-goat/scripts/telegram_push.sh` — the sanctioned urgent carve-out named
in `notif_enqueue.sh`'s own header ("Urgent paths … still call
telegram_push.sh directly"; verified present + executable) — via a new
fail-soft `_telegram_push_urgent` sibling mirroring `_telegram_push`'s
subprocess/timeout/never-raise shape with an
`EPM_TELEGRAM_PUSH_URGENT_SCRIPT` test override. **`realert`** stays on the
digest queue, keeping volume sane and criterion 3's arithmetic intact.
Acceptance criteria 2 + 4 now specify the channel; §Method delta carries the
latency arithmetic; new test `test_daemon_liveness_channel_split` asserts the
per-event routing and that no event fires both.

### Should-Fix 2 — docstring execution-order sentence

The lint (`check_asw_docstring_pass_count`) deliberately does not pin the
per-tick order, so omitting it would stay green but leave the canonical
enumeration internally incomplete. **Applied:** v3 also updates the
order sentence (`… 20 (program-orchestrator recovery) -> 40
(daemon-liveness) -> 13 (auth-outage guard) …`).

### Should-Fix 3 — save-before-emit (storm guard)

A persistent state-SAVE failure with a working LOAD would recompute
`consecutive == threshold` every tick and re-fire `open` (~6 pushes/hr) —
the v2 fail-safe claim covered the load side only. **Applied:** the save moves
BEFORE the emit, so a persistent save failure degrades to stderr + sidecar
only, matching the stated fail direction. Pinned by a new test (save forced to
fail on every tick of a 5-tick outage → `open` fires at most once).

### Should-Fix 4 — invariant-test channel collision

Raise-patching `subprocess.run`/`Popen` would also sever the push helpers'
own shell-out, so the sketched invariant test could not simultaneously assert
pushes fired. **Applied:** raise-patches are reserved for the mutation
surfaces (`_stop_session`, spawn helper, `task.py post-marker`); pushes are
pinned with recorder monkeypatches.
